standard_prerequisites: closed immersions of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces correspond to surjective morphisms B -> A in WAdm^Noeth (Formal Spaces, Lemma formal-spaces-lemma-closed-immersion-into-countably-indexed)

the completed naive cotangent complex of a quotient B -> A = B/J is the complex with J/J^2 in degree -1 (definition-rig-etale-homomorphism of the same chapter)
rig-smooth ring maps and the criterion that annihilation of J/J^2 by a power of I follows from rig-smoothness (definition-rig-smooth and lemma-equivalent-with-artin-smooth of the same chapter)
core_obligations: Prove that for a closed immersion f : X -> Y of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces the following are equivalent: (1) f is rig-smooth, (2) f is rig-etale, (3) etale locally on Y the map corresponds to a surjection B -> A in WAdm^Noeth whose kernel J satisfies I(J/J^2) = 0 for some ideal of definition I of B
proof_roadmap: Implication (2) to (1) is rig-etale implies rig-smooth.

For (3) to (2): the surjections B -> A occurring in (3) have completed naive cotangent complex equal to J/J^2 in degree -1, so the annihilation hypothesis makes them rig-etale by the definition, and the rig-etale criterion for morphisms transfers this to f.

For (1) to (3): rig-smoothness makes B -> A rig-smooth over (B, I); again NL^wedge is J/J^2 in degree -1, and the smooth variant of the equivalence lemma forces J/J^2 to be annihilated by some power I^n, which is itself an ideal of definition since B is adic.
difficulty_reason: H3: a three-clause equivalence discharged by reading the definitions of rig-etale and rig-smooth through the two-term cotangent complex of a closed immersion.
